title: Self-Control
definition: Self-Control is Spirit-enabled restraint and disciplined obedience in desires, words, habits, and actions.
summary: Self-Control is Spirit-enabled mastery over desires, impulses, habits, and reactions under the lordship of Christ.
christFocus: Jesus Christ gives freedom from slavery to sin and forms disciplined holiness in His people by the Spirit.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content: This doctrine focuses on ordered desires. Self-control is not mere personality strength; it is fruit of the Spirit that teaches the believer to say no and yes at the right time. It applies to appetites, speech, anger, sexuality, spending, entertainment, and attention.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content: This matters because desires make poor masters. Without self-control, freedom turns into bondage and witness is damaged. This doctrine gives hope that grace trains believers to live disciplined, wise, and fruitful lives.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Identify one area where desire regularly outruns obedience. Put practical boundaries in place while depending on the Spirit, not willpower alone. Celebrate small acts of obedience as real grace at work.
